 J U D G M E N T

The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation amount of Rs.30,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are as under:
On 7.4.2018 at about 3.30 p.m. the petitioner was traveling along with her family members from Hassan towards Tumkur in a car bearing No.KA-53-ME-5829, which was driven by one Nanjundaswamy with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human lie and safety of others, when he reached near Joddagatte Rajesh Dhaba, Bidar to Srirangapatna road, Turuvekere in order to avoid oncoming lorry he suddenly took the left and dashed against the road side tree.
Due to the said impact, the car was severely damaged and the petitioner and her family members sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately she was shifted to Adichunchanagiri hospital, further she was shifted to M.S. Ramaiah Hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she was treated as inpatient.

3. Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, he was hale and healthy,
aged about 43 years, doing agriculture and earning a sum of Rs.20,000/- per month.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-53-ME-5829.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Contending the above facts, he prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost.
4. In response to the petition notice, the respondents have appeared through their counsel, but inspite of sufficient opportunities given to the respondent No.1 has not filed his written statement

,
so, the written statement of the respondent No.1 is taken as not filed.
The respondent No.2 has filed its written statement.

5. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 are as under:
The respondent No.2 has contended in its written statement that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further admitted about the issuance of the policy and its validity from 11.10.2017 to 10.10.2018 and the policy is having coverage only for limited liability.

Further contended that neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied the mandatory provisions of S. 134 and S. 158(6) of the M.V. Act in furnishing the better particulars.
Further contended that driver of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to drive the same as on the date of accident.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition.
Contending the above facts, he prays to dismiss the claim petition as against this respondent with cost.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:

sentences.text: 1. Whether the petitioner proves that she had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing registration No. KA-53-ME-5829 on 7.4.2018 at about 3.30 p.m. near Joddagatte, Rajesh Dhaba, on Bidar-Sr.Patna Road, Turuvekere Taluk, Tumkur District?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3
. What order or award?

7. In order to prove the case, the petitioner herself has examined as PW1 and got marked the documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P15 and doctor is examined as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P16 & Ex.P17.
8.
To disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondent No.2 has not examined any witness on their behalf.
9. Heard the arguments.

10. My findings to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: In the Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:
R E A S O N S 11. ISSUE NO.1:- During the course of arguments, the learned counsel for the petitioner argued by reiterating the contents of petition and also evidence put forth by PW1 & PW2.
Further he argued that, to prove the disablement, the petitioner has examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. as PW2, who has assessed the disability of 89% of left lower limb and 29% of whole body.
Further he argued that the petitioner has proved his case as contended in the petition by producing oral and documentary evidence.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.

12. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has denied the accident in toto, hence,
prays to dismiss the petition.
13. On rival contention urged by both the counsel, I, intend to discuss the merits of the case.
14. In order to prove the case, the petitioner has examined herself as P.W.1 and she has stated in her evidence by reiterating the contents of petition.

Further in support of her evidence, she has produced the prosecution papers and the same are marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P5 such as FIR with complaint, spot mahazar, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet.
Smt.Kalpana vs Shri Nanjundaswamy on 3 September, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95839367/
3 15.
On perusal of Ex.P1 complaint reveals that complaint has been lodged by Thrinethrappa on 14.4.2018.

So, based on the complaint, FIR came to be registered by Turuvekere Police in Cr.
No.150/2018 against the driver of the car for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 337 of IPC.

Ex.P2 is the spot mahazar drawn by the I.O. also reveals the scene of incident, Ex.P3 is the IMV report reveals that the damages caused to the vehicle and IMV inspector has opined that the accident was not due to any mechanical defect of the vehicle.
Ex.P4 is the wound certificate reveals that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.

Ex.P5 is the charge sheet reveals that after investigation I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the lorry for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337,
338 and 304(A) of IPC.
16. The counsel for the respondent No.2 has argued that the alleged vehicle was not involved in the accident.
To substantiate the said facts, he has not examined any witness nor produced any documents to show that the alleged vehicle was not involved in the accident.
On the other hand, the petitioner has proved his case through oral and documentary evidence.

17. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others).

sentences.text: 18. Looking to the oral evidence of PW1 and the documents placed before the court, it is clear that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car.
Hence, I answer this issue in the affirmative.
19. ISSUE NO.2:-
The case of the petitioner is that she met with an accident on 7.4.2018 at about 3.30 p.m. and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately she was shifted to Adichunchanagiri hospital, wherein she took the first aid treatment, later on she was shifted to M.S. Ramaiah hospital,
wherein she was admitted as an inpatient.

To substantiate the said fact, petitioner has produced wound certificate at Ex.P4, which discloses the following injuries:
1)Contusion on left knee,
2)Contusion found of mid of left 20.
The doctor is of the opinion that the said injuries are grievous in nature.

The petitioner has produced copy of the discharge summaries marked at Ex.P6 to Ex.P11, which discloses that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took the treatment as inpatient from 7.4.2018 to 25.4.2018, from 15.5.2018 to 18.5.2018, from 28.5.2015 to 31.5.2018, 23.8.2018 to 30.8.2018,
14.12.2018 to 5.12.2018 and from 28.1.2019 to 29.1.2019.
21.

PW2 being the Orthopaedic surgeon has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained left leg tibial plateau fracture with proximal fibula fracture with Popliteal artery transaction with left leg compartment syndrome, and she was treated in the M.S.Ramaiah hospital, wherein she underwent left trans Popliteal Thrombectomy with primary vessel repair, faciotomy with AO Smt.Kalpana vs Shri Nanjundaswamy on 3 September, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95839367/
4 external fixator application on 8.4.2018 and later underwent left fasciotomy with AO external fixator application on 8.4.2018 and later underwent left leg fasciotomy and wound debridement twice and later the external fixator was removed and closed reduction and tibial plateau fracture fixation was done with cancellous screws with Illizarov external fixator and later discharged on 25.4.2018 and again she got admitted on 4.12.2018 for removal of femoral ring of the illizarov and discharged on 5.12.2018 and again on 28.1.2019 she got admitted for removal of tibial illizarov ring fixator.

He has produced clinical notes and x-ray marked at Ex.P16 & Ex.P17.
22.

Considering the oral evidence of PW1 & PW2 and the documents placed before the court, I am of the opinion that the petitioner might have sustained pain and agony, for which, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.70,000/- under the head of pain and sufferings.
23. The case of the petitioner is that, he was hale and healthy at the time of accident, aged about 43 years and doing agriculture and getting an income of Rs.20,000/- per month.
But she has not produced any documents pertains to her avocation and income.
In the absence of the documents pertains to her avocation and income, it is very difficult to assess the income of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition.

So, considering the present life condition and the age of the petitioner,
if notional income of Rs.8,500/- per month is considered, it will meet the ends of justice.

The petitioner has produced copy of the discharge summaries marked at Ex.P6 to Ex.P11, which discloses that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took the treatment as inpatient from 7.4.2018 to 25.4.2018, from 15.5.2018 to 18.5.2018, from 28.5.2015 to 31.5.2018, 23.8.2018 to 30.8.2018, 14.12.2018 to 5.12.2018 and from 28.1.2019 to 29.1.2019.
The petitioner has sustained grievous injuries; she might have taken rest and treatment at least for six months.
Therefore, six months income comes to Rs.51,000/- is granted to the petitioner under the head of loss of income during laid up period and rest period.
24. The contention of the petitioner is that, she has spent huge amount of Rs.15,00,000/- towards medical expenses.

Out of the said amount Rs.1,28,639/- has been paid by New India Assurance Company under Medi Assit insurance policy and remaining amount has been paid by her and she has produced reimbursement letters marked at Ex.P12.
On perusal of Ex.P12 one of the bill is not belongs to the petitioner.
On record she has produced the medical bills marked at Ex.P15 to the extent of Rs.10,61,518/-.
The petitioner herself has stated in her chief- examination that she took the reimbursement from the Media Assist Insurance TPA Pvt. Ltd. a sum of Rs.1,28,639/-.

entities.text: Media Assist Insurance TPA Pvt. Ltd.
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: So, after deducting Rs.1,28,639/- from the amount of Rs.10,61,518/- it comes to Rs.9,32,879/-.
Therefore, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.9,32,879/- towards medical expenses.
25. Further contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy, aged about 43 years, doing agriculture and earning Rs.20,000/- per month.

Due to the accident, she is not able to climb or descend stairs, she cannot bend her body, she cannot stand for long duration,
she cannot stand firmly, cannot move from one place to another without any help and she has become disabled.

The petitioner has produced photographs at Ex.P14 and one CD at Ex.P14(a).
26.
To prove the age, the petitioner has not produced any document.
On perusal of discharge summary the age of the petitioner is mentioned as 40 years.

The petitioner herself has mentioned in Smt.Kalpana vs Shri Nanjundaswamy on 3 September, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95839367/
5 her petition that he age was 43 years at the time of accident.
So, same is considered as the age of the petitioner as on the date of accident.

27. PW2-Dr.Nagaraj has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and recently he has examined on the petitioner and assessed the disability of left lower limb is 89%
and whole body is 29%.
On perusal of cross- examination he has stated that fracture is united.

So,
considering the evidence of PW2 and the cross-examination and the age and avocation of the petitioner and relative disability, if 20% of the disability is considered as whole body of disability of the petitioner, it will meet the ends of justice.
The petitioner age is already considered as 35 years the multiplier applicable to this age is 16.
Considering the above facts, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.2,85,600/- under the head of loss of future earning.
29. Further contention of the petitioner is that she has sustained grievous injuries.
So her happiness and pleasure will be restricted to some extent through out her life.
Hence, it is just and necessary to award compensation of Rs.20,000/- under the head of amenities.
30. PW1 has stated in her evidence that due to the accident he took the treatment as inpatient.

She has produced the discharge summaries marked Ex.P6 to Ex.P11, which discloses that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took the treatment as inpatient from 7.4.2018 to 25.4.2018, from 15.5.2018 to 18.5.2018, from 28.5.2015 to 31.5.2018, 23.8.2018 to 30.8.2018, 14.12.2018 to 5.12.2018 and from 28.1.2019 to 29.1.2019, which discloses that petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took the treatment as inpatient.
The petitioner has produced taxi bills to the extent of Rs.29,550/-, which is marked at Ex.P13.
So, one must attend her during the above said period and she has spent some amount towards conveyance.

Considering the above facts and looking to the period of hospitalization, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.40,000/-
under the head of attendant, conveyance, food and nourishment etc.
31.

Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:
 Sl.No. Compensation heads Amount  1. Pain and suffering Rs. 70,000-00 2.
Loss of income during laid period Rs. 51,000-00 and rest period 3.

Medical expenses Rs.9,32,879-00 4. Loss of future income Rs.2,85,600-00 5. Loss of amenities, Rs. 20,000-00 Smt.Kalpana vs Shri Nanjundaswamy on 3 September, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95839367/
6 6. Attendant, Nourishment and Rs. 40,000-00 conveyance charges Total Rs.13,99,479-00 32.
LIABILITY:

On perusal of the contents of petition and contents of written statement, it reveals that, the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the car bearing No.KA-53-ME-5829.
33.
The respondent No.2 has admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.KA-53-ME-5829 and its validity.
Therefore, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 8% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 in partly affirmative.
34. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of above discussion on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of MV act is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.13,99,479/- with interest @ 8% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with interest at 8% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of compensation amount together with interest, 40% of the amount shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner in any nationalized/scheduled bank for a period of three years and remaining 60% of the amount shall be released to the petitioner through account payee cheque on proper identification without any further proceedings.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer online, corrected by me and then pronounced in open court on this the 3rd day of September 2019).
(MAHANTESH S.DARGAD) III ADDL.SMALL CAUSES JUDGE & ACMM, BANGALORE.
